title: Playmobil Christmas edition – what drives monthly sales? (exam 2019/20)
text: To maximise their share of kids' allowance, Playmobil analysed monthly toy sales of its "Christmas edition" box sets: number of retail outlets (outlet_number), promotional spending online, on billboards and on TV, the box's age suitability (box_age: 4+, 5+, 6+) and the number of pieces in the box as an indication of size (box_size).
y = β0 + β1·outlet_number + β2·online_spend + β3·billboard_spend + β4·TV_spend + β5·box_age + β6·box_size

title: H&M – forecasting 2022 sales (mock exam, revision session)
text: An analyst at H&M forecasts sales considering the number of retail outlets (outlet_number), promotional spending online, on billboards and on TV, sales from the previous year (old_sales) and the average number of new product launches (new_products).
y = α + β1·outlet_number + β2·online_spend + β3·billboard_spend + β4·TV_spend + β5·old_sales + β6·new_products + ε

title: Grocery shopping – refined model (practice case, fictitious coefficients)
text: A U.S. supermarket models customers' total annual grocery spending (USD). After dummy-coding gender (female = 1), loyalty programme membership (member = 1) and region, a refined model with four predictors is estimated. All coefficients shown are significant (p < 0.05); adjusted R² = 0.54.
